title: Finite biproduct equivalence for primary curve assertions
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $k$ a field, $X$ a scheme and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.
Let $I$ be a finite index type and $G_a$ module sheaves on the small etale site of $X$.
Let $H$ be a module sheaf equipped with an isomorphism $e:H\simeq\bigoplus_a G_a$,
using finite biproducts [def-weil-additive-category]. The predicates $C_1,\ldots,C_8$
are those of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions], with their stated conditional hypotheses.
Let $r$ be prime and suppose $r\operatorname{id}_{G_a}=0$ for every $a$ and
$r\operatorname{id}_H=0$. Then $C_3(H)$ holds if and only if $C_3(G_a)$ holds for every $a$.
Primary torsion has the geometric-stalk meaning of [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion].

source.place: Theorem 03SC, proof, fourth paragraph; Lemma 0A5C. Primary text checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SC and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A5C.

proof.text: Let U be the additive functor forgetting module coefficients, and T_q = U followed by Mathlib Sheaf.functorH in degree q. For every q, H^q(H) is subsingleton iff every H^q(G_a) is. Forward, map the retraction G_a -> H -> G_a given by injection followed by e.inv and e.hom followed by projection. If T_q(H) is zero, its mapped identity composite is zero, hence T_q(G_a) is zero. Reverse, map the biproduct identity sum_a pi_a >> iota_a; every summand factors through a zero T_q(G_a), so the identity of T_q(biproduct G) is zero. Map e to transport this identity to T_q(H). The empty index case is the empty sum identity. AddCommGrpCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton converts zero objects to subsingletons. This uses only additivity and the finite biproduct identities, without an Ext product equivalence or derived-global-sections bridge.
Apply prime_annihilated_primary_cases to H and to every G_a. Each is r-primary; if any one is p-primary for a prime p different from r, that sheaf is zero.

Unfold C3, fix a prime p with CharP k p, a primary-torsion hypothesis and q > 1. If r = p, use the r-primary witnesses from the preceding step and the degreewise subsingleton equivalence in the first step, in each direction. If r differs from p, the sheaf for which the conclusion is required is zero by the preceding step; U.map_isZero and Mathlib Sheaf.subsingleton_H_of_isZero give vanishing. No affine, proper, or curve hypothesis is used.

proof_origin.place: Stacks 03SC, proof, fourth paragraph and 0A5C; P2 Lean realization using additive biproduct identities and existing prime-annihilated primary cases.

theorem prime_biproduct_primary_iff (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (r : ℕ) [Fact r.Prime] {ι : Type} [Finite ι]
    (G : ι → Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (hGr : ∀ a, r • 𝟙 (G a) = 0)
    {H : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)} (e : H ≅ ⨁ G)
    (hHr : r • 𝟙 H = 0) :
    VanishingAboveOneOfIsPrimaryTorsionSheaf Λ H k ↔
      ∀ a, VanishingAboveOneOfIsPrimaryTorsionSheaf Λ (G a) k
